title: tool-calling: ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection, and retries
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: improve developer ergonomics for multi-tool workflows and parallel tool invocations while preserving streaming stability and OpenAI function-calling compatibility. This PR introduces a clearer execution model for tool calls: 1) a ParallelToolExecutor that can run multiple tool calls concurrently with configurable concurrency limits and backpressure, 2) explicit tool result injection semantics that allow the runtime to insert tool outputs into the LLM context as 'injected_result' entries while preserving deterministic token offsets for streaming clients, and 3) a retry policy framework for transient tool failures with per-tool backoff and idempotency hints. The change preserves compatibility with the current OpenAI-style 'function_call' field but adds an opt-in 'execution_hint' field to request synchronous injection vs deferred tool-handling. Implementation summary: core runtime changes in serving/runtime/tool_executor.go and serving/runtime/streaming_injector.go add the execution primitives, API layer changes in redwood-api/handlers/tool_calling.go and openai-compat/openai_tool_adapter.go add the new request/response fields and translation logic, SDK updates in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript add helpers for parallel tool orchestration and idempotency tokens. Testing: unit tests for retry/handoff logic and concurrency limits, integration tests exercising streaming stability with injected results, and a perf canary demonstrating tail-latency impact under parallel workloads. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains the same for existing clients; new fields are opt-in. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4821) [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] SDK helpers shipped [x] perf canary + benchmark results attached. Commits: see commits field for a concise list. Review summary: addressed requested clarifications around token accounting for streaming clients and added an opt-in mode for deterministic offsets. Merge: squash-merged after two approvals and green CI.
release_notes: Adds opt-in parallel tool execution primitives, deterministic streaming result injection semantics, and configurable retry policies for tool calls. Backwards compatible by default.
